The second is exactly the pre-2026-09-04 device the design is reasoned about &mdash; the record&rsquo;s own words, *&ldquo;on an old device &lsquo;absent from pending&rsquo; means &lsquo;never pushed&rsquo;&rdquo;*. **DRIVEN:** with `bld_sync_pending` absent and the server provisioned, trust is granted on the FIRST load with zero pushes. **THE CONSEQUENCE IS DELAYED BY ONE CONDITION NOBODY DESIGNED FOR IT.** `mayOverwrite` is `pend.state==='ok' && !__overflow && bldPendingTrusted()`, and on that first load `state` is `absent`, so nothing is overwritten and the device looks fine. The `state==='ok'` term exists to handle an UNREADABLE map; it is not part of the trust design and it is currently the only thing between a wrongly-granted flag and data loss. **DRIVEN END TO END, three steps, nothing unusual:** (1) old device, one local edit made before the mechanism existed and never pushed &mdash; load 1 grants trust and merges additively, so nothing looks wrong; (2) any later write fails, `bldPendingMark` writes the key, state becomes `ok`; (3) next load, `mayOverwrite` is true and the never-pushed edit is replaced &mdash; measured, the note goes from &ldquo;EDITED HERE, never pushed&rdquo; to &ldquo;the server copy&rdquo;. The Cost Code Roll-up hardcodes its percentage to 0 when there is no budget, so a cost code with $5,000 committed against no budget rendered **"$5,000 / $0 · 0%" with a zero-width bar in critical red** — the colour and the number, same row, saying opposite things.
